attribution_limitations: Table 1 reports whole-tumor medians (including fluid voxels) and changes relative to baseline, whereas the Results text reports solid-voxel changes and a t5 versus t4 comparison (for example MD +23.6%, FW +30.7%, DTI-FA -34.9%, FWI-FAt -3.3%). The text values and table values are different measurements and are not merged. The DTI-FA and FWI-FAt sentence cites Table 1, but Table 1 prints neither -34.9% nor -3.3%, and the sentence states no region or time of its own; the reference point of the solid-voxel MD and FW percentages is also not stated.

In the parsed table text each Q1/Q3 cell of Table 1 shows two numbers run together (for example 0.1040.214, 0.10.181). The original article XML prints each cell as two values separated by a line break, Q1 above Q3, so the split recorded in the quartile facts follows that printed break, not a digit-count convention. The measurement series excludes these cells because its cells come from the run-together text.
The follow-up is described as 8 months (abstract and Methods) while Table 1 gives 269 days from treatment start for t5; the stated intervals are approximate and not treated as a conflict.
Tumor pseudoprogression is only suggested as a possibility ("potentially indicate"); the 34% rate in the same sentence is a published cohort figure and not a patient fact.
Patient sex is not stated and age is given only as a range.

Structural and diffusion MRI sessions at baseline and 9, 17, 24 and 30 days after treatment start showed a stable tumor volume with a T2w signal increase, a rise in fluid voxels at t1 with falling FA and FAt and rising MD and FW in solid voxels, then smaller fluid-voxel changes while the solid-voxel trend progressively inverted.

evidence.quote: underwent PBT six months after partial tumor resection
PBT was delivered in 30 daily conventional fractions of 1.8Gy relative biological effectiveness (RBE) for the total target cumulative dose of 54Gy
The PBT was well-tolerated.
Macroscopic tumor and target volume during treatment were monitored using structural MRI (T1-weighted or T1w, FLAIR, T2-weighted or T2w) and dMRI
Even though during treatment the mass showed a T2w signal increase, its volume remained stable (compared to the baseline: mean Dice coefficient of overlap: 0.95; mean relative volume change: 5.35%).
Before the PBT, the tumor presented with 7.6% fluid voxels (Figure 2A), which at t1 increased by 88.5%

In the solid voxels, at t1, the FA and FAt decreased whereas the MD and FW increased

claims.text: At the 8-month follow-up (t5), the T2w signal remained high, the tumor volume increased to 44.7 cm^(3), and fluid voxel number and diffusivity increased. Vomiting, headache and ideomotor slowing at t5 were effectively treated with corticosteroids. The authors suggested possible tumor pseudoprogression, and the normal-appearing white matter showed changes strongest near the tumor.

In the solid voxels at t5, there were increases both in the MD (+23.6%) and in the FW (+30.7%).
At t5, the patient presented with vomiting, headache, and ideomotor slowing, which was effectively treated with corticosteroids.
At t5, the increases in the total tumor volume, fluid volume, and diffusivity, reflect the observed signal increase in the T2w image and potentially indicate tumor pseudoprogression
The NAWM showed microstructural changes at t5 that were the strongest in proximity to the tumor
